options: A separately installed program outside the Salesforce platform
A curated, named bundle of tabs, logo, and color built for a specific job function
A type of custom object
The mobile version of Salesforce only
questions.explain: In Salesforce, an app is a lightweight concept: a named, curated set of tabs plus branding, tailored to a job function like Sales or Service — not a separately installed program.

questions.q: What happens to your data and permissions when you switch from one app to another?
options: Your data and permissions reset to default
You are logged out and must sign back in
Nothing changes — only which set of tabs is displayed changes
You switch to an entirely different Salesforce org
questions.explain: Switching apps only changes which curated set of tabs is in front of you — your data, your org, and your permissions stay exactly the same.

questions.q: What is the App Launcher, informally called 'the waffle'?
options: A report type
A field on the Account object
A Setup-only tool unavailable to regular users
The grid-of-dots icon used to switch between apps and search for objects
questions.explain: The App Launcher is the small grid icon (nicknamed 'the waffle') that opens a quick panel for switching apps or searching for any object you have access to.

questions.q: What does the 'All Items' list on the full App Launcher page show?
options: Only the items in your current app's tab bar
Every object you have access to, even ones not shown in your current app's tabs
A list of deleted records
A list of other users in your org
questions.explain: The full App Launcher page's 'All Items' section lists every object you have access to — useful for reaching an object that isn't exposed in your current app's tab bar.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Lightning Experience and Salesforce Classic?
options: They are two names for the exact same interface
Classic is a newer beta version of Lightning Experience
Lightning Experience is the current, modern interface; Classic is the older interface being phased out
Classic is only used for custom objects, and Lightning only for standard objects
questions.explain: Lightning Experience is Salesforce's current, modern interface, which replaced the older Salesforce Classic interface — Classic is still technically available in some orgs but is being steadily phased out.
